plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own) if you win. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to you, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to adjust for, and this being a one-shot auction, I will bid exactly my private value of $46 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're highest). Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to adjust for, I'll bid exactly my private value of $17 to guarantee optimal expected profit this round.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding above your value risks paying more than the item is worth to you, while bidding below reduces your chance of winning without any benefit. With a value of $28, I should bid exactly $28 to maximize expected profit.
